Where You Will Work

Located approximately 50 miles northeast of Safford, Arizona on U.S. Highway 191, Morenci operations (an open-pit copper mining complex) has been in continuous operation since 1939. The operation consists of two concentrators, crushed-ore leach pad and stacking system, a low-grade run-of-mine (ROM) leaching system; four SX plants; and three EW tank houses that produce copper cathode.

High School diploma or GED and two (2) years related experience in supporting field maintenance or operations department within a mining/mfg environment, OR

TRC, Member of WSP, is a global consulting environmental and engineering firm and one of the top design firms in the energy sector. Together, TRC and WSP’s 83,000 experts create positive, long-lasting impacts for our communities and our clients in the power and energy, transportation and infrastructure, environmental, and property and buildings sectors. From pipelines to power plants, roadways to reservoirs, schoolyards to security solutions, clients look to TRC for breakthrough thinking backed by the innovative follow-through of an industry leader.

We recognize that the expertise of our staff is our strongest asset, so we generously reward employees for successful performance and invest in their careers through training and the development of new skills and certifications.

TRC is looking for an experienced GIS Analyst to join its delivery team and support the development and execution of industry leading solutions for some of North America’s largest utilities customers. In this role you will work directly with our customers, our technical teams, and industry partners to position for, respond to, and deliver solutions.

jobs.title: Digital Customer Success Program Manager
jobs.description:
About Us

STACK is a leading provider of cloud-based construction estimating and takeoff software solutions, committed to helping businesses transform through innovative solutions. We pride ourselves on fostering a collaborative, dynamic environment where team members have the opportunity to grow and make a real impact.

About The Role

STACK is looking for a Digital Customer Success Program Manager to build the digital Customer Success motion that reaches every customer, whether or not a CSM is assigned to them. We have thousands of single-seat customers and a growing base of larger accounts. Human coverage alone won't get all of them to adopt STACK and see value from it.

Your job is to design, build, and run the programs that do – in-app sequences, scaled training, email campaigns, and whatever other channels the customer journey calls for.

This is a cross-functional role. You'll partner with Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success to define the motion, then work with our onboarding and consulting team to deliver training and with CS Operations to make it measurable. You'll own the programs end to end: the customer journey they support, the content that goes into them, the tooling that delivers them, and the numbers that tell you whether they worked.

What You’ll Do

Design the Digital Success Motion

Partner with Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success to design, develop, and deliver STACK's digital Customer Success motion.
Map the customer journey from onboarding through renewal and expansion and define the moments where a digital program should do the work.
Decide which channel fits which moment and recommend new channels when the journey needs one.
Define where digital coverage stands on its own, where it supports CSM, and where a human must take over.
Build the program calendar so customers get coordinated experience rather than competing messages from three teams.

Build and Run In-App Programs

Own in-app engagement in Pendo: guides, sequences, walkthroughs, announcements, and in-product nudges.
Use product usage data and behavioral signals to target the right customers with the right prompt at the right point in their workflow.
Build in-app onboarding and feature adoption paths that move customers to their next meaningful action.
Test, measure, and iterate on guide performance, and retire what isn't working.
Partner with Product on in-app messaging standards so the experience stays clean and useful, not noisy.

Scale Training and Education

Build multiple learning paths for different customer roles, products, and stages of maturity.
Partner with Marketing to develop and produce the training content, and with our onboarding and consulting team to deliver it.
Stand up the tracking behind training consumption: who enrolled, who finished, what they did in the product afterward.
Turn repeatable one-to-one onboarding and consulting work into scaled, self-serve programs.
Keep the curriculum current as STACK's platform and AI capabilities evolve.

Own Email and Campaign Programs

Build lifecycle email programs that drive onboarding, adoption, education, retention, and expansion.
Partner with Marketing on segmentation, content, design, and deliverability, and keep customer messaging coordinated with campaigns already in flight.
Trigger campaigns from product signals and customer health, not just from a calendar.
Run a real testing rhythm on subject lines, timing, audience, and offers, and act on what the tests tell you.

Measure What's Working

Define the success metrics for every program before it launches: engagement, adoption, consumption, retention, and expansion impact.
Partner with CS Operations on the data, tooling, and reporting the programs need.
Report on program performance to CS leadership and the wider business, and be direct about what didn't work.
Use the results to decide where to invest next and where to stop spending effort.

Partner Across STACK

Work with Customer Success to make sure digital programs support CSMs instead of duplicating their work.
Work with Marketing on content, campaign execution, brand, and voice.
Work with Sales on the customer segments, renewal moments, and expansion plays the programs should support.
Work with the onboarding and consulting team on training delivery and on what customers struggle with most.
Bring customer feedback and program insights back to Product and CS leadership.

The Channels You'll Work In

these are the channels we're building on now. Part of your job is telling us what's missing.
In-App (Pendo): Guides, sequences, and product nudges targeted by usage and behavior.
Scaled Training: Role-based learning paths built with Marketing, delivered by onboarding and consulting, with consumption tracked.
Email Campaigns: Lifecycle and signal-triggered programs across onboarding, adoption, retention, and expansion.
Your Recommendation: Webinars, communities, help content, video, or whatever else the journey needs. Make the case and build it.

What You Bring

Direct experience delivering digital Customer Success programs. You've built scaled or tech-touch programs before and can point to what they changed.
3+ years in Customer Success, customer marketing, lifecycle marketing, customer education, or a similar program role, ideally in SaaS.
Hands-on experience with an in-app engagement platform. Pendo is a plus, but Gainsight PX, Appcues, WalkMe, or similar counts.
Experience building customer learning paths or education programs, and tracking whether customers actually consumed them.
Experience running lifecycle email programs in a marketing automation or CS platform.
Comfortable with data. You can segment an audience, read a funnel, and tell the difference between a program that drove adoption and one that just got clicks.
A strong writer who can turn a product capability into copy a busy customer will act on.
Proven at working across Marketing, Sales, CS, Support, and Product without formal authority over any of them.
Organized enough to run several programs at once and keep them on schedule.
Curious about AI, and interested in using it to make programs more personalized and faster to build.
Comfortable in an environment where the playbook isn't finished and you're expected to help build it.
Experience in construction, preconstruction, real estate, or another vertical SaaS market is a plus, but not required.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role means customers get a useful, well-timed experience from STACK whether or not a person is assigned to them. You'll know you're doing the job well when:

Single-seat and long-tail customers are adopting STACK and renewing without a CSM touching every account.
In-app programs are moving customers to their next action, and you can show which ones do it best.
Training reaches customers at scale, and we know who consumed it and what changed in their usage afterward.
Email programs run off customer signals and health, not a fixed calendar.
CSMs use digital programs as leverage on their own accounts instead of working around them.
Marketing, Sales, and CS are working from one coordinated customer journey.
Every program has a metric, a result, and a clear decision about what happens next.

Why Join STACK?

We're at an exciting point in the company's growth and at the forefront of bringing AI and modern technology into preconstruction. This role is a rare chance to build a digital Customer Success motion from the ground up, for a customer base big enough that the work matters on day one.
If you like designing programs, running them yourself, and proving what worked, we'd love to hear from you.
Opportunity to work in a fast-paced, growth-oriented, remote-first environment.
Async-friendly environment with a focus on ownership and deep work.
Be part of a dynamic, supportive team where your contributions are valued.

At STACK, our values shape how we work, collaborate, and serve our customers:

Radical Honesty: Communicate directly, respectfully, and transparently—even when conversations are difficult. Give and receive feedback with care.
Customer Obsession: Put the customer at the center of every decision. Solve real problems, follow through, and measure success by customer outcomes.
Move With Purpose: Take thoughtful action, remain accountable, and own both successes and mistakes. Anticipate what’s next and adapt as you learn.
Grow Together: Share knowledge, collaborate across teams, and invest in one another’s development. Celebrate collective wins and treat setbacks as opportunities to learn.

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. We are committed to building a team that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. The more inclusive we are, the better our work will be.

We are interested in every qualified candidate who is eligible to work in the United States. However, we are not able to sponsor visas.

We take into account an individual’s qualifications, skillset, and experience in determining final salary. This role is eligible for health insurance (medical, dental & vision), life insurance, 401(k) & paid time off. The expected compensation range for this position is about $112k-130k + quarterly bonus. Hi! We're Forerunner.

Stronger, more resilient communities are built by the people inside government and regulated industries who keep critical infrastructure running. But they're working against real headwinds: fragmented data, field crews without the right tools, and high-stakes decisions made without a complete picture.

Forerunner exists to fix that. We build intelligent software that connects the systems these agencies and firms already rely on, fills the gaps those systems can't, and turns fragmented information into decisions and actions that reduce liability, surface revenue, and prevent small problems from becoming emergencies.

About The Role

As a Customer Success Manager, you will own the ongoing success of a full book of business — from onboarding through renewal — ensuring every account realizes measurable value from Forerunner and grows into a durable, trusted partnership. You'll work at the intersection of relationship management, product adoption, and account growth, partnering with Sales, Product, and Engineering to keep outcomes on track.

What you'll do

Customer Health & Retention

Serve as a trusted advisor to your accounts, understanding their workflows and goals well enough to guide them toward renewal.
Own customer health across your portfolio, using data and regular check-ins to catch risk early and keep accounts moving toward measurable outcomes.
Guide customers through public-sector and regulated-industry decision cycles with patience and clear communication.

Product Adoption

Partner with the Deployment Specialist to take a clean handoff at go-live and carry momentum into the ongoing success phase.
Drive adoption through user communications, customized in-app onboarding, and continued learning so customers get full value from their investment.
Configure customer environments and settings as needs evolve, using both the product front end and Forerunner's internal tools.

Account Growth

Identify and pursue expansion opportunities — upsells, add-ons, and cross-sells — within your accounts.
Partner with Sales and leadership to build the case for expansion and drive it to close.

Cross-Functional Partnership

Share customer feedback, ideas, and concerns with Product and Engineering to inform the roadmap.
Evangelize customer success stories across your accounts to help build the broader Forerunner community.

Team Building

Contribute to the ongoing development of CS policy, process, and playbooks as an early member of a growing team.

What we're looking for

4-6 years of professional experience in customer success, account management, or client services, with a track record of managing end-to-end renewals and proactively uncovering expansion opportunities within a portfolio.
Experience serving government agencies or regulated industries — GovTech, floodplain management or flood insurance, GIS/mapping, or public-sector project management are all relevant backgrounds, though not required.
Comfortable managing complex, public-sector relationships and decision cycles; experience partnering with government clients or supporting complex public-sector workflows is a plus.
An excellent, empathetic communicator — you're often a customer's first point of contact, and building trust matters in our space.
Detail-oriented and committed to quality, with genuine enthusiasm for creating customer value.
Comfortable with a high degree of ambiguity — able to prioritize independently and take on responsibility as the team grows.
Experience supporting SaaS software is preferred but not required.

You'll thrive in this role if you...

Believe in delivering measurable outcomes to customers, not just checking off tasks.
Enjoy being a trusted point of contact and building long-term relationships.
Are comfortable balancing day-to-day account management with longer-term account strategy.

Our team has a lot to offer.

Forerunner is an early-stage company with an interdisciplinary team. We are motivated by seemingly intractable problems and work hard to support one another.

We're mission-driven. Our mission orients our business strategy and pushes us to work with a sense of urgency. We're in the weeds — our entire team spends time engaging with our partners in the field to better understand the real-world problems they face.
We're a small team. As a member of our growing team, you will quickly become an invaluable part of our organization and have a meaningful impact on our business and technical direction. We welcome unique perspectives and backgrounds. Your opinion matters and we hope you'll share it.
We build each other up. A team works best when its members are equipped with the tools to tackle the problems they're facing. Forerunner strives to provide meaningful feedback and learning opportunities to help all our team members grow.
We value in-person connection, so we keep offices in NYC, San Francisco, and Portland, ME. Roles can be hybrid or fully remote, depending on the work.
We want you to be happy and healthy. Forerunner offers competitive compensation, health/vision/dental coverage, a 401k plan, and one expensed lunch per week. We also have a quarterly wellness reimbursement so you can define what "health" means to you.
The salary range for this position is $90,000-$120,000 with an OTE of $105,000-$135,000. This posting may span more than one career level. Compensation is determined based on a variety of factors, including an individual's skills, experience, and qualifications.

jobs.description:
About Us

MintMCP helps companies put agents to work safely. We exist to help companies do more of their work with agents, and we build the infrastructure that makes a company's own work runnable by them. Our product gives those agents governed access to company data and tools. That has to start from trust.

Before agents can touch Slack, GitHub, Jira, Snowflake, internal databases, or production systems, you need to know what they can reach, what they did, and why they were allowed to do it. Most people carry far more permissions than any single task needs. If an agent uses your token directly, it inherits all of them. MintMCP scopes that access down to exactly what an agent needs to do its job and captures the data flows and audit logs security teams need. From there we are building the rest of the agent stack: connectors, monitoring, sandboxing, long-running agents, and memory, with the goal of becoming the system a company's work runs on.

We work in person in the San Francisco Bay Area. The structure is flat and the market moves fast, so you have a lot of latitude over what you work on and how.

We are AI-native. Everyone uses Claude and Codex every day, and we have more agents than employees. They run in Slack alongside the team and handle sales, marketing, deal ops, and engineering on the same gateway we sell to customers, and we are building an entire company operating system around them.

Since launching in February 2026, we have grown to 50+ paying customers, with strong inbound demand. Customers include Coursera, Arlo, and Braze. We are backed by Cowboy Ventures and Coatue, with angels including Frederic Kerrest (Okta), Michael Grinich (WorkOS), Andrej Karpathy, Jeff Dean, and Scott Belsky. Our founders are machine learning experts from Stanford, Berkeley, and CMU, with applied research at Google Brain and Waymo, and one co-founded Coursera.

The job

You own the customer once the deal is signed, all the way through. On day one that means building the mutual delivery plan with the customer: what success looks like, who does what, and by when. You drive onboarding, get the product live against real use cases, and stay close as usage grows. You are the person the customer trusts to make their rollout work.

From there you own the whole arc. You track account health, run the check-ins and business reviews, catch problems before they become risks, and pull in engineering or the founders when a customer needs more than you can give them alone. You own renewals, and you find and grow expansion, more teams, more agents, more of the company's work running on us. When something is on fire, you are the one who owns getting it resolved.

You'll also push in both directions. On the customer side, that means telling them when what they've asked for isn't what they need, and reframing it against what we've seen work elsewhere. Internally, it means advocating for your customers clearly and directly to the founders — while weighing what they want against what the company needs to prioritize. We'd rather you argue with us than quietly agree with a customer.

You are our first dedicated post-sales hire, so you also build the function. You turn what works into a repeatable motion: the delivery plan template, health scoring, the review rhythm, the handoff from sales. As the customer base grows, you help decide who we hire next and grow into leading customer success. The role is in person, with travel to meet customers.

About You

You are exceptional with customers. People trust you quickly, and you keep a rollout on track without being told to. This is the core of the job.
You have owned customer relationships end to end, in customer success, account management, consulting, or a client-delivery role.
You can run a plan and drive it to an outcome across a customer's team, aligning stakeholders, tracking commitments, and keeping momentum.
You are comfortable in technical conversations without being an engineer. You can hold your own with a technical buyer, explain what the product does and why it matters, and know when to pull in the team for the deep end. You do not write config or debug integrations.
You have carried retention and expansion, or have the commercial instinct to, and can point to relationships you kept and grew.
You have built structure where there was none, playbooks, templates, cadences, and you would rather build the motion than inherit one.
You are calm under pressure and own the outcome when a customer is unhappy.
You are AI-native, or will get there fast, and are genuinely curious about AI, agents, and how companies adopt them.
You move fast without a lot of process, and you want to grow into leading a team.

Nice to have:

AI solutions engineer or forward-deployed engineer background.
You've sold to or supported technical and engineering buyers.
Experience with enterprise rollouts where security review, procurement, and multi-threading are part of the relationship.
Comfort representing the company in person: business reviews, dinners, and on-site meetings with technical and security leaders.

What we offer

Competitive base, variable, and significant equity.
Full ownership of your accounts, with room to build the function and grow into leadership.
Direct access to the CEO, customers, and product decisions.
Health benefits, on a team that puts family and health first.

new_jobs.description:
About Us

MintMCP helps companies put agents to work safely. We exist to help companies do more of their work with agents, and we build the infrastructure that makes a company's own work runnable by them. Our product gives those agents governed access to company data and tools. That has to start from trust.

Before agents can touch Slack, GitHub, Jira, Snowflake, internal databases, or production systems, you need to know what they can reach, what they did, and why they were allowed to do it. Most people carry far more permissions than any single task needs. If an agent uses your token directly, it inherits all of them. MintMCP scopes that access down to exactly what an agent needs to do its job and captures the data flows and audit logs security teams need. From there we are building the rest of the agent stack: connectors, monitoring, sandboxing, long-running agents, and memory, with the goal of becoming the system a company's work runs on.

We work in person in the San Francisco Bay Area. The structure is flat and the market moves fast, so you have a lot of latitude over what you work on and how.

We are AI-native. Everyone uses Claude and Codex every day, and we have more agents than employees. They run in Slack alongside the team and handle sales, marketing, deal ops, and engineering on the same gateway we sell to customers, and we are building an entire company operating system around them.

Since launching in February 2026, we have grown to 50+ paying customers, with strong inbound demand. Customers include Coursera, Arlo, and Braze. We are backed by Cowboy Ventures and Coatue, with angels including Frederic Kerrest (Okta), Michael Grinich (WorkOS), Andrej Karpathy, Jeff Dean, and Scott Belsky. Our founders are machine learning experts from Stanford, Berkeley, and CMU, with applied research at Google Brain and Waymo, and one co-founded Coursera.

The job

You own the customer once the deal is signed, all the way through. On day one that means building the mutual delivery plan with the customer: what success looks like, who does what, and by when. You drive onboarding, get the product live against real use cases, and stay close as usage grows. You are the person the customer trusts to make their rollout work.

From there you own the whole arc. You track account health, run the check-ins and business reviews, catch problems before they become risks, and pull in engineering or the founders when a customer needs more than you can give them alone. You own renewals, and you find and grow expansion, more teams, more agents, more of the company's work running on us. When something is on fire, you are the one who owns getting it resolved.

You'll also push in both directions. On the customer side, that means telling them when what they've asked for isn't what they need, and reframing it against what we've seen work elsewhere. Internally, it means advocating for your customers clearly and directly to the founders — while weighing what they want against what the company needs to prioritize. We'd rather you argue with us than quietly agree with a customer.

You are our first dedicated post-sales hire, so you also build the function. You turn what works into a repeatable motion: the delivery plan template, health scoring, the review rhythm, the handoff from sales. As the customer base grows, you help decide who we hire next and grow into leading customer success. The role is in person, with travel to meet customers.

About You

You are exceptional with customers. People trust you quickly, and you keep a rollout on track without being told to. This is the core of the job.
You have owned customer relationships end to end, in customer success, account management, consulting, or a client-delivery role.
You can run a plan and drive it to an outcome across a customer's team, aligning stakeholders, tracking commitments, and keeping momentum.
You are comfortable in technical conversations without being an engineer. You can hold your own with a technical buyer, explain what the product does and why it matters, and know when to pull in the team for the deep end. You do not write config or debug integrations.
You have carried retention and expansion, or have the commercial instinct to, and can point to relationships you kept and grew.
You have built structure where there was none, playbooks, templates, cadences, and you would rather build the motion than inherit one.
You are calm under pressure and own the outcome when a customer is unhappy.
You are AI-native, or will get there fast, and are genuinely curious about AI, agents, and how companies adopt them.
You move fast without a lot of process, and you want to grow into leading a team.

Nice to have:

AI solutions engineer or forward-deployed engineer background.
You've sold to or supported technical and engineering buyers.
Experience with enterprise rollouts where security review, procurement, and multi-threading are part of the relationship.
Comfort representing the company in person: business reviews, dinners, and on-site meetings with technical and security leaders.

What we offer

Competitive base, variable, and significant equity.
Full ownership of your accounts, with room to build the function and grow into leadership.
Direct access to the CEO, customers, and product decisions.
Health benefits, on a team that puts family and health first.
